title: A platform worker can show substitute earnings and a formal remedy while receipt and durable access remain open
source_unit: One adjudicated Fair Work Commission platform-worker case, UDE2025/141 / PR792727
geography: Australia; comparative case used to test the platform-remedy stage of the US-centered atlas

observations.period: 2025-06-13; platform deactivation and subsequent substitute-work period

baysec_substitute_earnings.unit: AUD received for work performed after deactivation

didi_post_deactivation_earnings.unit: AUD across the following four months as described by the Commission

didi_extrapolated_pre_deactivation_earni.unit: AUD across the comparable extrapolated four-month period

observations.method: Case-level extraction from the Commission merits decision; substitute earnings were used in the lost-pay calculation.
observations.uncertainty: The public decision does not observe alternative-work availability, hours, expenses, net income, conditions, or whether the routes were freely chosen rather than necessary.
observations.subgroup: One named worker with adjudicated platform deactivation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Substitute earnings establish an observed alternative-work route, not equivalent work, restored security, or a preferred choice.

observations.method: Case-level extraction from the Commission re-filed order and associated merits decision.
observations.uncertainty: An order and deadline are not payment receipt, actual account reactivation, durable protection, or later work.
observations.subgroup: Same named worker case after formal adjudication.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal remedy authority can coexist with unobserved implementation; the passage of a deadline is not evidence of payment.

denominator.unit: named worker case and public search route

later_continued_use_or_exit_observed.unit: public later-use, switch, non-use, or exit records located

observations.method: Targeted official Fair Work Commission search across the merits decision, re-filed order, bulletin, and decisions/orders route; absence is coded as public non-observation, not private non-occurrence.
observations.uncertainty: A public-search non-observation cannot establish that payment, access, or later work did not occur privately.
observations.subgroup: Same named worker case after the order.
observations.counterinterpretation: The case advances alternative-work and formal-remedy stages but does not close receipt, recovery, durability, trust, or practical exit.

related_sources.claim: Bounded machine recheck preserving case stages, official URLs, and non-observed implementation fields.
Official bulletin route checked for later implementation evidence.

boundary: This is one comparative Australian adjudicated case, not a worker prevalence estimate or a US population result. It closes an observed substitute-earnings stage and a formal remedy-order stage for one worker, but not freely chosen alternatives, payment receipt, actual account restoration, durable protection, household recovery, trust, political action, or practical exit.
